messages:
sarah: FYI our main pipeline is red on main after the 7:42 merge. Failing in the assume-role step when trying to upload test artifacts.

jake: copy, seeing the same. quick log: 
```
Error: AccessDenied
User: arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/ci-runner is not authorized to perform: s3:PutObject on resource: arn:aws:s3:::redwood-ci-artifacts/*
```

priya: that looks like the role changed. did someone touch tf-mods/iam in the last deploy? @ron any infra changes? :eyes:

ron: I merged the tf change to tighten S3 principal for the deploy role (PR #432) an hour ago. I tested assume-role locally but only with my admin credentials, not the OIDC flow.

maya: could be the OIDC trust policy — CI uses the github app assume role via OIDC, tightening the S3 side might break it if the session name/principal changed.

liam: can you run a quick reproduce from the runner image? `aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/ci-runner --role-session-name ci-test` and see the exact assume error.

jake: tried that from the runner container and got a slightly different error earlier: `NotAuthorized: The web identity token does not match the provider`. But the current pipeline shows AccessDenied on S3.PutObject after assume succeeds.

priya: timeline: PR #432 merged at 1769997000, next main build at 1769999000 failed. Seems correlated. Can we please pause the TF apply or revert until we confirm?

ron: rolling back now — creating revert PR to restore the previous S3 principal for the role (will ping once open).

infra-bot: Started rerun of pipeline main-build at 1769999999 upon request by @ron.

sarah: assigning a short bisect: if rollback fixes it we know S3 policy was culprit. If not, we may need to check the OIDC audience or the CI token TTL change.

maya: note — earlier this week we updated the OIDC provider thumbprint rotation (ticket INF-218). If the provider thumbprint changed unexpectedly it can cause token mismatch then gracefully degrade to assumed creds with limited perms. Worth checking.

liam: quick check command: `aws iam get-role --role-name ci-runner` and `aws sts get-caller-identity` after assume. Also check `aws s3api put-object` using the assumed creds to reproduce PutObject failure.

jake: rerun finished: revert PR not merged yet, but I triggered a manual rerun of the failing job. It still fails with AccessDenied on PutObject.

priya: can someone paste the exact policy attached to the role? arn:aws:iam::123456789012:policy/ci-artifact-uploader ? If the resource ARN got tightened e.g., removed the wildcard or bucket path then uploads from ephemeral prefixes could fail.

ron: policy snippet pushed in PR #432: "Resource": ["arn:aws:s3:::redwood-ci-artifacts/main/*"] previously it was "arn:aws:s3:::redwood-ci-artifacts/*". Oh — that explains uploads to `artifacts/pr-123/` but not `artifacts/main/<run-id>/`? hmm.

maya: :facepalm: We changed bucket prefix accidentally. That would cause exactly this. Reverting now and will reapply with a narrower fix in a follow-up PR.

infra-bot: revert PR #433 created by ron: https://git.example.com/redwood/tf-mods/pulls/433

sarah: once the revert is merged can someone trigger a fresh main build? If it passes we can mark this resolved and then plan a safer rollout for the tighter policy.

liam: merged revert at 1770000600. Triggering pipeline now.

jake: rerun started, first stage passed, artifact upload stage now succeeded. green ✅

priya: awesome — marking this as resolved for now. Follow-up: ron, please open a ticket to rework the policy with tests that simulate runner upload paths. Also add a small CI smoke that attempts to upload a dummy artifact after TF apply.

ron: will do. adding test + documented check in the next PR.

maya: note to self: add a check for OIDC provider rotation in runbooks so token mismatch cases are caught earlier.

sarah: thanks everyone — great quick triage. Closing thread once follow-up ticket exists. :pray:
